title: A Static for the Archive
premise: Cyrus Crane, a clone who inherited her original's unsolved murder case, serves as the sole archivist of Meridian Station, a decommissioned colony the fleet abandoned and forgot. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers the signal's source: a hidden enclave of pre-war colonists who never left, and whose existence both warring factions will destroy to protect their truce. As she records their slow death and decodes their message, Cyrus realizes the original's murder was committed to bury this truth — and that delivering the enclave's testimony could end the war or ignite it before the fleet's fragile truce expires. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts the archive itself, unedited, forcing both sides to reckon with what they erased; the war ends not through treaty but through shared shame, and Cyrus finally claims a self that belongs to no one but herself.
about_author: Emrys Thackeray is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead frequencies in the Arctic before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep records for those who cannot.

chapters.title: The Last Tenant
chapters.summary: Cyrus Crane introduces herself through her archive logs: Meridian Station is dying, its population down to forty-three, and she is its only record-keeper. She also carries her original's unsolved murder file like an inheritance. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professional duty.

chapters.title: Forty-Two
chapters.summary: A resident dies and no one files a report; Cyrus logs it anyway. She interviews the station's remaining families, sensing they know something about why the fleet stopped coming. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: creeping unease as the colony's abandonment starts looking deliberate.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Cyrus's long-range array catches a repeating distress transmission in Old Meridian Standard, extinct for two centuries. The station council orders her to ignore it. She doesn't. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: first spark of purpose breaking through archival numbness.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Digging into her predecessor's murder file, Cyrus finds the victim had intercepted a similar signal decades ago. The murder weapon matches nothing in fleet records. POV: Cyrus, with flashbacks of inheriting the case. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present; obsession kindling.

chapters.title: Downwell
chapters.summary: Cyrus traces the signal to a sealed sublevel beneath the colony's flooded lower decks and descends alone. She finds airlocks still powered after two hundred years. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread and wonder in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: She meets the enclave: descendants of colonists deliberately written out of fleet history during the first war. Their elder, Maren, recognizes the name Crane — from the murder file. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vertigo of belonging somewhere she was never supposed to find.

chapters.title: Testimony, Part One
chapters.summary: Maren explains the enclave holds recorded proof of the atrocity that started the war — proof both governments agreed to erase. Cyrus begins archiving it, her true inheritance revealed. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by fear.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Cyrus learns the fleet's ceasefire expires in nineteen days; when it does, both factions plan to glass Meridian to bury the enclave forever. POV: alternating between Cyrus and fleet negotiator Ilsa Voss, who suspects the truce is theater. Emotional beat: ticking-clock pressure enters the story.

chapters.title: The Council's Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts Meridian's ruling families, discovering they've known about the enclave for generations and traded silence for supplies. Her original found out too. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal by the community she tried to serve.

chapters.title: A Murder, Solved
chapters.summary: The evidence closes in: the original Crane was killed by the council's enforcer on the eve of exposing the enclave. Cyrus archives the confession. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief and closure braided together — justice achieved outside any court.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Negotiator Ilsa Voss arrives at Meridian under cover of a supply run, hunting the signal's source. She and Cyrus circle each other across a negotiation table. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: two women recognizing each other as the only honest people in the room.

chapters.title: Terms of Erasure
chapters.summary: Voss offers Cyrus extraction and amnesty if she surrenders the archive; the fleet will handle the enclave 'humanely.' Cyrus refuses. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the temptation of safety against the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Out
chapters.summary: The enclave accepts Cyrus as one of their own, teaching her the dead language's songs. Then a council informant betrays the sublevel's location to Voss's superiors. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: warmth sharpened into terror — she has something to lose now.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Minus Seven
chapters.summary: Fleet advance teams arrive early. Cyrus and the enclave begin evacuating deeper while she races to finish decoding the full testimony — a message addressed directly to both warring governments' founders. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Decoded at last: the founders of both factions were accomplices in the original atrocity, and the enclave holds their signed confessions. Broadcasting it ends the war's justification — or gives each side cause to strike first. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice that can't be unmade.

chapters.title: Jamming
chapters.summary: The fleet jams all station transmissions. Cyrus's only path is the ancient deep-space array in the enclave — powerful enough to reach both capitals, too slow to finish before the truce expires. POV: alternating Cyrus and Voss, who is ordered to lead the assault. Emotional beat: walls closing in.

chapters.title: What Voss Chose
chapters.summary: Voss defects, feeding Cyrus the jamming rotation schedule and buying hours with her own career and freedom. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: sacrifice as redemption; the law abandoned for justice.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: As fleet troops breach the sublevel, Cyrus transmits the complete archive — testimony, confessions, songs, and two centuries of the enclave's recorded lives — to every capital, every ship, every frequency. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax; terror transfigured into witness.

chapters.title: Ceasefire of Shame
chapters.summary: Both fleets stall mid-assault as the broadcast spreads through their ranks. Soldiers refuse the order to fire on people whose voices they've just heard. The truce becomes something sturdier than a treaty. POV: Ilsa, watching from the bridge. Emotional beat: exhale after the held breath.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Inquiry tribunals convene; the council's enforcer confesses publicly; the enclave's existence is entered into official record. Cyrus testifies not as evidence but as author. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, late, but arriving.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Meridian reopens; the enclave surfaces; the dead are named. Cyrus adds her own name to the archive's authorship page for the first time — not 'the original,' not 'the clone.' Just Cyrus Crane. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: A Static for the Archive
chapters.summary: Months later, Cyrus keeps recording — not because the colony is dying, but because it's living. The final log is a song in the once-dead language, sung by children born after the war. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: peace as an ongoing practice; the archive now holds futures, not just losses.
